name: maybe_Field_InitDescriptorFromConst
signature: void maybe_Field_InitDescriptorFromConst(u32 actor, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Copies the 24-word constant block at 0x007291F0 onto the stack and sets a state byte (2 when the 50-entry named-row table still has a free row, else 3). The entry point is half bad-instruction data and the surviving code is a descriptor-template copy, so nothing here builds a table.
evidence: Disassembly 0x0021066C: the first half is flagged as bad instruction data (halt_baddata), and the rest is Game_GetWork -> 0x0066B1FC(work+0x24A98) -> state 2/3 plus a 24-word copy of 0x007291F0 into the frame; the old 'BuildActorTable' wording described a guess, not the code.

name: maybe_Actor_ActionSeq_RunChoice
signature: u32 maybe_Actor_ActionSeq_RunChoice(ActorActionSeq* self, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Action-sequence node step: branches on the pending-command mask at self+0x3534 (bits 0x142/4/0x10/1) and then asks the page object at self+0x3574 to switch to action kind 3/5/6/7/9/10/0x0C/0x10 according to the result (0..3) of selector 0x006509AC; always returns 1.
evidence: The mask tests and the selector's 0..3 result are explicit in the body, and each branch issues a page request through vtable+0x14 followed by vtable+0x10. Still no caller and no vtable slot, so the 'choice node' reading stays an inference.

name: maybe_Actor_ActionSeq_RunAction1B
summary: Issues action 0x1B through the object's vtable+0x54 and then reads the game work; everything after that failed to decompile, so only the action id and the virtual call are real.
evidence: Disassembly shows the indirect call with 0x1B and then invalid instructions (unaff_r6/unaff_r10, in_NG/ZR/OV, halt_baddata); no new caller or neighbour resolves the tail, so the confidence floor is unchanged.

name: maybe_Ui_CloseChildIfFinished
signature: int maybe_Ui_CloseChildIfFinished(UiObject* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Ticks the child object at self+0x1B4 (virtual+8) and, when its finished query (+0xC) returns true, sets bit 0 of the 101-entry save flag array at (work+0x24A98)+0x5762 for id 0x12 and returns 0; otherwise returns self.
evidence: 0x00612550 is not a UI-manager notify: its disassembly is cmp r1,#0x65; add r0,r0,r1; ldrb/orr #1/strb [r0,#0x5762], i.e. mark one id in the 101-byte flag array. The control flow of 0x002DF358 (tick child -> finished -> set flag -> return 0) is unchanged.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_FinishIfBusy
summary: If the widget at self+0x11C reports busy (vtable+0x14) it is told to finish (vtable+0x10); 64 bytes, same two-call idiom as 0x00316568 and 0x003175E0.
evidence: The Game_GetWork call is only the 8-byte stack-alignment prologue (its result is discarded) and the two indirect calls are +0x14 then +0x10; no caller, vtable slot or string identifies the class, so 'Window' stays a generic label.

name: Ui_WorldMapMarker_ApplyVisitedFlags
summary: Applies the per-map visited flags to the 25 world-map marker slots: for slot 0..24 it copies the save flag from 0x0066B45C(bagWork, slot) into bit 0 of the marker pane's +0x44 flag (so unvisited markers are hidden). Same loop as Ui_WorldMapMarker_UpdateVisited without that function's parent-update prologue.
evidence: 0x0066B45C disassembly is a pure bit test (cmp r1,#0x19; lsr/and on the 25-bit mask at (work+0x24A98)+0x3AE0), and this body is the second half of the already-named Ui_WorldMapMarker_UpdateVisited (0x003A7E4C, 0.50): same 0x120 base, same 0x50 stride, same 25 iterations, only the parent-update call is missing.

name: Ui_ListWindow_RemoveSourceRowAt
summary: Deletes row `index` from the 50-entry, 0x8C-byte row table at (work+0x24A98)+0x5FE4: the rows behind it shift down one slot and the freed last row is zeroed with a 0xFFFFFFFF key.
evidence: Named caller Ui_Window_StartAction4Or2 dispatches it as a list action, and 0x00612F5C's disassembly is a memmove of (0x31-index)*0x8C bytes upward over the row at index followed by clearing entry 49 - an index-based row delete, not a flag setter.

name: Party_AppendBlankMemberRecords
summary: Calls Party_List_InsertBlankRecord(bagWork) `count` times: that helper shifts the 0x2A0-byte party-record array at bagWork+0x9400 up one slot and installs a freshly blanked record at the front, so this appends `count` empty party members.
evidence: The callee is the already-named Party_List_InsertBlankRecord (0x00193018), and the loop runs exactly `count` times on work+0x24A98; the old 'UI party list insert' reading of 0x00193018 is superseded by the 0x2A0-stride record shift.

name: maybe_Actor_ConfirmSelection
signature: bool maybe_Actor_ConfirmSelection(void* self, int index, int value)
summary: If `index` equals the panel's current selection (self+0x497) it applies it: takes the member id from the child object at +0x768, resolves the member record, calls the inventory-slot helper 0x00190270(member,index,value), sets member+0x12E0/+0x12E2 to 0xFF and notifies the owner (self[0x48B]) with code 4; returns whether the index matched.
evidence: 0x00190270 sits inside the Member_* inventory blob (7 bytes after Member_RemoveItemAtSlot at 0x001901F4, where Ghidra merged split symbols), so the value's exact meaning is still unproven; the member plumbing is clear but the caller is still an unnamed action-sequence step.

name: maybe_Ui_MapIcon_AddIfFlagSetA
signature: void maybe_Ui_MapIcon_AddIfFlagSetA(void* self, int flagId, int slot)
summary: Icon-stack builder (variant A): while fewer than three icons are placed it tests one of three global flags (0x0066B088 accepts only flagId < 4 through 0x0066B8B0); a clear flag hides the pane at self+slot*4+0x7C, otherwise the next entry's position (self+count*4+0x70, fields +0x1C/+0x20/+0x24) is copied into that pane, the pane is shown and the count at +0x88 is incremented.
evidence: Both callees are now readable as small flag helpers (0x0066B8B0 combines three byte arrays into bits 0..2 and 0x0066AF34's blob tests one bit), so flagId is a 0..3 category index rather than a map id. No caller and no vtable slot tells which icon class this copy serves.

name: maybe_Ui_MapIcon_AddIfFlagSetB
signature: void maybe_Ui_MapIcon_AddIfFlagSetB(void* self, int flagId, int slot)
summary: Byte-identical twin of 0x003D20E8 (same 172 bytes): places up to three icons, hiding the pane when the 0..3 category flag for flagId is clear and otherwise copying the next stack entry's position into it and bumping the count at +0x88.
evidence: Same body as 0x003D20E8 (template copy, FACTS 'identical bodies'); the flag id is bounded to 0..3 by 0x0066B088, so it is a category index, not a map id. Neither copy has a caller, so which icon class this instance serves is unknown.

name: Ui_TextFormat_SetMemberNameAndIds
summary: Fills message argument slots 2, 8 and 9 from the member behind self->f_208: slot 2 gets the padded name (+0xCA, strlen+1 clamped to 0x7F wchars) and slots 8/9 get '%d' of self+0x210/self+0x214, each formatted by std_String_FormatInitG into the slot's 0x80-byte inline buffer before the slot pointer is repointed.
evidence: Disassembly 0x003D8FF0 writes exactly base+0x218/pointer+0x214 (slot 2), base+0x848/pointer+0x844 (slot 8) and base+0x950/pointer+0x94C (slot 9) on *0x007AC834, and the family's reset callee is the named Message_FormatArgSlot_Reset, so the slot indices in the name are verified rather than inferred.

name: Ui_TextFormat_SetMemberNameAndItemText
summary: Sets message argument slot 2 to the member name (+0xCA, padded/truncated to 0x7F wchars) and slot 5 to the display text of the id at self+0x210 (Item_LookupRecord then Text_FormatMessageArg), i.e. a 'member got item' message.
evidence: The disassembly calls Item_LookupRecord on self+0x210 and Text_FormatMessageArg before repointing slot 5, and slot 2 is written like its confirmed sibling 0x003D8FF0. The Item_LookupRecord call only supplies the item's display name: this is text formatting, not item/inventory logic.

name: Ui_TextFormat_SetMemberNameAndValue
summary: Sets message argument slots 2 and 8 from the member behind self->f_208: slot 2 gets the padded name ('%ls', +0xCA) and slot 8 gets '%d' of the u8 at member+0xD8, both formatted into the slots' inline buffers (*0x007AC834 + 0x218 / + 0x848).
evidence: Disassembly writes slot 2 (+0x218/+0x214) and slot 8 (+0x848/+0x844); the %d source is member+0xD8 (the byte after the 7-wchar name), matching the family's slot layout and the named Message_FormatArgSlot_Reset callee.

name: Ui_TextFormat_SetMemberNameSlot
signature: void Ui_TextFormat_SetMemberNameSlot(void* self, int slot, u32 memberId)
summary: Formats the name of the member `memberId` (+0xCA, strlen+1 clamped to 0x7F wchars) into message argument slot `slot` through Message_FormatArgSlot_Reset + std_String_FormatInitG, i.e. the generic 'put this member's name in text slot N' setter.
evidence: The only tail call is the named Message_FormatArgSlot_Reset with the caller's arg2 as the slot index and the padded member name as the value, while the siblings 0x0041200C/0x003D8FF0 hard-code slots 2/8/9; 0x00100B74 is wcslen, which is why the readable C looked truncated.

name: Ui_TextFormat_SetMemberNameAndTwoValues
summary: Sets message argument slots 2, 8 and 9 for the member behind self->f_208: slot 2 the padded name (+0xCA), slot 8 '%d' of the byte at (self->f_A8 + 0xB105) and slot 9 '%d' of the byte at +0xB106, all into the slots' inline buffers.
evidence: Disassembly writes the same three slot offsets as 0x003D8FF0 (+0x218, +0x848, +0x950) but takes the two numbers from the sub-object at f_A8; the named Message_FormatArgSlot_Reset family and the shared '%ls'/'%d' format calls confirm the role.

name: maybe_Ui_ChildTransform_CreateRowChildren
summary: Creates up to 32 numbered child panes from the ASCII digit template at 0x007BFA7E: it increments the trailing digits with carry, builds each pane through the layout factory (vtable+0x2C of self->f_A8), stores the pointers after the u16 id pair at self+0xB64, and hides the children whose bit is clear in the mask returned by 0x0066B64C(bagWork, f_B64, f_B66).
evidence: The digit-increment loop and the 0x20 (32) cap are explicit in the body, and 0x0066B64C is now readable (it builds a key from f_B64/f_B66 and searches the 8-byte-stride table at bag+0x3220). Which list hosts the 32 numbered rows, and why the world-map rebuild call precedes it, stay open - there is no caller or vtable slot.

name: maybe_Battle_Action_TestFlag80OrMemberHandFlag
signature: u8 maybe_Battle_Action_TestFlag80OrMemberHandFlag(void* unit, int hand, u8* action)
summary: Battle action predicate: requires unit+0x10 and action+0x10 to be non-zero, then returns true when the spell id at action[0] resolves to a record whose +0x2E8 has bit 0x80 set (or, when action[0] is 0xFF, the skill id at action[1] resolves to +0xFF with bit 0x80), and otherwise falls back to the acting member's per-hand byte +0xDED (hand 0) / +0xDEE.
evidence: Disassembly 0x0048833C: ldrb [r0,#0x10] / ldrb [r2,#0x10]; bl 0x18C184 (spell record) -> ldrb [r0,#0x2E8] & 0x80; bl 0x18C1B8 (skill record) -> ldrb [r0,#0xFF] & 0x80; then member+0xAF0+0x2FD/0x2FE. The old 'Monster' prefix was wrong - the fallback reads the party-member record, and nothing identifies the 0x80 bit's meaning yet.

name: maybe_Ui_MonsterBook_BuildDetailPane
summary: Builds the monster-book detail for one monster: resolves the monster record (0x0063E5C8), matches its two name-message ids against key[0], requires the book record's +0x22 counter (0x0063DCA4) and the per-monster word at (work+0x24A98)+0x3AE4+id*4, copies the book message text (0x0063A46C), selects the 2D sprite (0x0028DDB0), animates the panes (0x001A6680) and fills the same message slots as the Ui_TextFormat family.
evidence: 0x004A3DA0 is a vtable slot at 0x007755CC (rodata dump) and its callees are the monster-record lookup, Text_CopyMessageLine, Ui_SpriteSpan_Select, Ui_Pane_PlayLayoutAnim and the monster-book display-mode getters 0x0024272C/0x00242754 used by the named Ui_MonsterBook_BuildEntryList/Ui_MonsterBook_SelectModel. The old 'LogFormat' came from the wcslen-truncated body and matched nothing.

name: Party_Member_KnowsSpell
summary: Returns 1 when the member's spell list (u8[40] at member+0x1274, terminator 0xFF) contains spellId; when the caller passes member id 3 it first remaps it to 27 (0x1B) through the 123-bit lookup at (work+0x24A98)+0x3AD0.
evidence: 0x006291EC counts the non-0xFF bytes at member+0x1274 (the u8[40] spell list established in FACTS) and 0x006298E0 returns member[0x1274+i]; the loop compares those ids with the third argument. The old 'Party_HasItem' was wrong - it never touches the 24-item inventory at member+0xEC.

name: maybe_Casino_SetSpinRateConstant
summary: Stores the float constant 600.0f (0x44160000) into the caller's float slot and mirrors it to work+0x2DEE0; called by the casino slot speed step.
evidence: Disassembly: vldr s0,[pc] (600.0f); vstr s0,[r0]; ldr r0,[r0]; str r0,[work+0x2DEE0]. The only caller is maybe_Casino_Slot_UpdateSpeed, and nothing here installs a gimmick context - the old name described a guess.

name: maybe_Work_TestEmptySlotA
summary: Thin wrapper that returns the result of 0x0066AAD0(work+0x2FB18, 0), the empty/occupied test of slot 0 in the table at work+0x2FB18. The declared void return is Ghidra's; the callee's r0 is passed straight back.
evidence: Disassembly: push {r3,lr}; Game_GetWork; add r0,work,#0x2FB18; mov r1,#0; bl 0x66AAD0; pop {r3,pc}. It returns a value (r0 unchanged), and the body is identical to 0x004B01CC - no auto-mode flag is written.

name: maybe_Work_TestEmptySlotB
summary: Same body as 0x004AFB64: returns the result of 0x0066AAD0(work+0x2FB18, 0), the empty/occupied test of slot 0 in the table at work+0x2FB18.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x004AFB64 (template copy, FACTS 'identical bodies'); disassembly is Game_GetWork -> 0x0066AAD0(work+0x2FB18,0) -> pop {r3,pc}. It returns a value (r0), so no gimmick flag object is created.

name: maybe_Work_GetU16FromTable2725C
signature: u16 maybe_Work_GetU16FromTable2725C(u32 arg1, int index, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Returns the u16 at work + index*2 + 0x2725C: a pure indexed getter into the u16 array that starts at work+0x2725C, immediately before the display block (work+0x27224..0x27254) copied by 0x0062AD8C.
evidence: The body is a single ldrh with no bounds check; the new neighbours place 0x2725C just before the actor display fields, but no caller names the array, so the generic 'table 0x2725C' wording is kept.

name: maybe_Ui_ScrollBar_IsRowDisabled
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_ScrollBar_IsRowDisabled(void* self, int row, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: For the row whose id byte sits at self+row+0x78 (ids are bounded to 0x65 by the callee), returns 0 when the corresponding flag byte in the 101-entry save array at (work+0x24A98)+0x5762 is non-zero and 1 when it is zero; the caller Ui_SakusenWindow_UpdateCounter uses it to skip unavailable rows.
evidence: 0x0066B3F8 disassembly is cmp r1,#0x65; ldrb r0,[r0+r1,#0x5762] (the same array 0x00612550 sets), and the body complements the byte, so this is a per-row availability test, not scrollbar geometry. It returns a value (u32), which is why the void-looking stub is safe.

name: Ui_TextFormat_SetMemberNameArg
summary: Formats the name (+0xCA) of the member behind self->f_208 into message argument slot 2 (record base *0x007AC834 + 0x218, pointer at +0x214), appending a second string when self+0x20C > 1 and truncating to 0x7F wchars.
evidence: Disassembly 0x004D6350 writes exactly one slot (std_String_FormatInitG at *0x007AC834+0x218, pointer stored at +0x214) and uses the same name-padding prologue as the confirmed slot-2/8/9 writers. Nothing is thrown - the old 'ThrowMissingMemberName' name came from the wcslen-truncated readable body.

name: maybe_Work_TestQuestStateInSet
summary: Predicate over the per-quest state array at work+0x2A4E6 (= (work+0x24A98)+0x5A4E): for quest id key[1] < 0x138 it returns 1 when the state byte is 1, 4 or 5.
evidence: The id is range-checked against 0x138 (the 312-quest table documented in FACTS) and indexed into work+0x2A4E6; the old 'ItemState' name was wrong - this is the quest-state table that 0x0064C7E0 also reads. What states 1/4/5 mean is still unknown.

name: maybe_Actor_FillDisplayParams
signature: void maybe_Actor_FillDisplayParams(void* self, void* out, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Fills the caller's display-params struct from the global display block: a header u16 from work+0x27C5C, tag byte 0xFF at out+0x40, then the fields work+0x27224..0x27254 into out+0xC..+0x3C and work+0x27C60 into out+8.
evidence: Both callers (ActorGetRegionBookID and maybe_Ui_MapWindow_RefreshEntry) consume the struct, and every source field comes from the work+0x27218 display block that 0x004A4ADC also counts; the layout is now readable but the struct's real use is still inferred.

name: Party_Member_GetAttack
summary: Returns (float)member->+0x1A for the member id stored in unit->f_768; +0x1A is the party member's Attack stat.
evidence: Disassembly: ldrh r0,[member,#0x1a]; vmov s0,r0; vcvt.f32.u32 s0,s0 - a float return in s0 that Ghidra dropped. FACTS records +0x1A = Atk in Party_Member_RecalculateStats, so 'GetFloatStat1a' can take its real name.

name: maybe_Ui_ListRow_GetRowClass
signature: u8 maybe_Ui_ListRow_GetRowClass(void* self, u32 rowIndex, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Shared row query with 225 call sites: returns 0xFF when rowIndex is out of range or the list model (self+0x24C) is missing, 0x15 when either global display-mode byte (work+0x27508/+0x27509) is set, and otherwise the row's own byte at +0xB (rows are 0xC bytes under model+0x58).
evidence: The 148 named callers (Battle_SelectAiActions, Ui_CmdQueue_ProcessSlots, Battle_BackupUnitActions, ...) all treat the result as a row state/class, and the body reads model+0x60 (count) / model+0x58+0x24 (row base) with a 0xC stride. The body is damaged (in_ZR/in_CY), so 'HeightClass' is downgraded to the neutral 'RowClass' and the confidence stays below 0.5.

name: maybe_Work_HasAnyNamedRow
summary: Returns whether the 20-entry, 0x8C-byte row table at (work+0x24A98)+0x7B3C holds at least one valid record; the callee counts rows whose name is shorter than 7 wchars and whose +0x88 key is not -1.
evidence: 0x0066B19C disassembly: 20 iterations, wcslen<7 plus u16[rec]!=0 plus [rec+0x88]!=-1, incrementing a counter; 0x006426A8 only tests count != 0 and returns a value (bool), so the void signature is only Ghidra's. The old 'Field_IsLoading' was unsupported - nothing here touches a loader.

name: Item_HasSpecialRangeItem
summary: Returns 1 when the player owns any of the 33 ids 0xA82..0xAA2, tested as bits 0..0x20 of the 33-bit mask at (work+0x24A98)+0x294C.
evidence: Callee 0x0066AD5C disassembly: sub r1,#0xA82; cmp r1,#0x21; bit test on the u32 mask at bag+0x294C, so the loop 0xA82..0xAA2 is exactly a special-range ownership check; the body returns a value (1/0) - the void signature is Ghidra's - and the twelve field-gimmick callers branch on it.

name: maybe_Ui_BagList_GetRowState
summary: Maps the per-id state byte at work+0x2A4E6 + row->f_298 to a list-row state: 0 for values 1 and 4, otherwise 3. 0x2A4E6 is the quest-state array base (bag+0x5A4E, 0x138 entries), so the row id has to stay below 312.
evidence: Caller is maybe_Ui_Overlay_GetCursorRowState's bag branch, but the index (row->f_298) has no range check and lands in the quest-state array at work+0x2A4E6 - the same table 0x005B144C reads with an explicit <0x138 guard - so whether the row really is a bag row is still open.

name: maybe_Ui_List_CountSelectableRows
summary: Counts the ids in the list [self+0xB0, self+0xB4) whose 90-bit save flag (0x0066B534, mask at bag+0x89A8) is clear and whose per-id byte at bag+0x3165 is below 10.
evidence: Both callees were read: 0x0066B534 is a 90-bit test on the mask at bag+0x89A8 and 0x0066AF08 returns bag[id+0x3165] (0xFF for id 0xFF). The 'selectable rows' reading survives, but nothing shows what the flag/byte pair means.

name: Party_GetSlotCountPlusPending
summary: Returns the number of occupied item slots (0..24) of the member whose id is at ctx+4, adding one when the pending-item flag at ctx+5 is set; 0 when ctx+4 is 0xFF.
evidence: Callee 0x00629150 disassembly counts the 24 u16 ids at member+0xEC that are not 0xFFFF (the member inventory established in FACTS), and the body adds 1 only while the count is <0x18 and ctx+5 is set - exactly the 'slot count plus pending' meaning.

name: maybe_Party_GetInventoryCountByIndex
signature: int maybe_Party_GetInventoryCountByIndex(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Returns the occupied-item-slot count (0..24) for the party record at index self+0x50, or 0 when that index is 0x1F or higher.
evidence: Same callee 0x00629150 (counts the 24 u16 inventory ids at member+0xEC that are not 0xFFFF) and the guard self->f_50 < 0x1F matches the 31-member roster; the old 'RecordSlotCount' did not say which slots are counted.

name: maybe_Work_FindFirstFreeSlot
summary: Returns the index of the first 0xFFFF terminator in the 90-entry u16 table at (work+0x24A98)+0x27C4, i.e. the first free slot of that table.
evidence: 0x0066B4F4 disassembly scans u16s from bag+0x27C4 to bag+0x2878 and returns the offset of the first 0xFFFF; the wrapper only adds the Game_GetWork prologue. The table's owner is still unknown, so the generic module stays.

name: maybe_Work_GetIdValueIfAtLeast
signature: u8 maybe_Work_GetIdValueIfAtLeast(u32 arg1, u8* query, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Conditional getter over the per-id 0x14-byte records at (work+0x24A98)+0x2D2D: query[0] is the id (0xFF means none), query[1] the minimum and query[2] the value; returns query[2] when record[id].byte0 >= query[1], else 0.
evidence: 0x0066B17C disassembly reads the byte at bag + id*0x14 + 0x2D2D (0xFF for id 0xFF), and the body then compares query[1] and returns query[2]. The 'Party' prefix was unsupported - this is a generic per-id record table.

name: maybe_Script_MakeNameHandle
summary: Builds a three-word tagged handle {nameId & 0xFFFFFF00 | 2, value, ...} for a script name-table id: validates the id through 0x0063D6FC (id -> record) and 0x0063D744 (record -> table), then range-checks record byte +1 against a random draw from the RNG at (work+8)+0x98; the second and third words come from registers Ghidra lost.
evidence: Caller Script_MakeNameHandleByIndex (0x00157B98) calls this for the real resolution and shares the 3-word layout; the tag 2 and the 0x7FFFFFFF rand bound are visible, but unaff_r6/unaff_r7 still carry two words, so no higher confidence.

name: maybe_BattleAi_PickRandomSpellTarget
signature: int* maybe_BattleAi_PickRandomSpellTarget(void* aiCtx, int spellId, int* arg3)
summary: Collects at most 16x6 candidate slots (16 unit buckets of 0x9BC bytes, 6 sub-slots) that spellId can hit (vtable+0xF8/+0xFC acceptance plus a per-slot state check through 0x004964C4), then returns one of them chosen with the battle RNG (func_001CA474(rng+0x4218, 0, count-1)); returns 0 when nothing qualifies.
evidence: Disassembly tail: cmp r7,#0 ; ldr r0,[*[gamWork+8]+0x5C]+0x4218 ; func_001CA474(rng,0,count-1) ; ldr [stack,r0*4]. The second argument goes straight into 0x0018C184 (the spell-record lookup), so it is a spell id, not a status priority.

name: maybe_Battle_RollCriticalHit
summary: Performs the critical-hit roll for one attacker: rejects units in states 8/10/0x10, requires the unit's +0x80 property (vtable+0xE8) to be clear and either member flag +0xDE9 or +0x11A9 to be set, then rolls the battle RNG in 1..100 and returns 1 when the roll exceeds 10.
evidence: Body is intact: func_001CA474(rng+0x4218,1,100), the constant 10, the two member flags and a 1/0 return (no multiplier); 'Modifier' is therefore downgraded to 'Hit'. Which passive +0xDE9/+0x11A9 is, and whether the threshold really is the crit rate, is still unknown.

name: maybe_SlotTable_CommitAndRetire
signature: void maybe_SlotTable_CommitAndRetire(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Commits the 0x50x5 slot table: clears the +0x2B0..+0x2EC bookkeeping words, copies every 0x2C8-byte row (5 sub-slots of 0x8C) from f_E8 to f_EC, resets the copied source rows to -1 sentinels/state 6, then retires committed rows whose member is in state +0xE4==5 or whose state byte at +0xB108 is 7 or 8.
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Menu_SumPartyStats on &self->f_47A0 (a menu sub-object) and the same 0x2C8/0x8C row layout is used by the field slot table 0x00174E40, so the 'Battle_' prefix was wrong; what +0xE4/+0xB108 mean is still unidentified.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_Step_DispatchFinishCommand
signature: int maybe_Battle_Ui_Step_DispatchFinishCommand(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Battle-UI sequence step: the countdown at +0x125C (reset to 0x102, -2 per call) gates a poll of the child widget (vtable+0x18); once the child reports idle it sends command 0x79 through Model_SetSlotState, sets the done byte +0xD2 and returns 1.
evidence: The +0x125C countdown / +0xD2 done-byte pattern matches the other battle step functions, and the 0x79 command plus the 3D-only animation func_005E7848 are visible in the body; no caller or vtable slot names the exact step, so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Actor_UpdateAnimState
